background:
Two liner-shipping firms consider forming a vessel-sharing alliance. Both must participate voluntarily. They share at least one market. Market complementarity concerns nonoverlapping market coverage and is distinct from compatibility of operating resources.

Unit: Potential alliance combination. Time horizon: Formation of the proposed vessel-sharing alliance.

Forecast the signed direction and strength of the relationship between Market complementarity between potential liner-shipping alliance partners and Observed vessel-sharing alliance formation.

Rate how higher market complementarity changes the likelihood that the firms establish a vessel-sharing alliance. Compare lower X (More overlapping market portfolios) with higher X (More nonoverlapping markets, retaining at least one common market). Use the same X contrast in both contexts. A positive rating means higher X is associated with more Y; a negative rating means less Y. Rate the relationship, not the overall level of Y. Do not interpret this judgment as a measured empirical coefficient.

Compare lower X (More overlapping market portfolios) with higher X (More nonoverlapping markets, retaining at least one common market). The X contrast and Y definition stay the same in both settings. Rate the relationship, not the overall level of Y.

The outcome is whether the potential vessel-sharing alliance forms, not the performance of an established alliance.

The lower-versus-higher market-complementarity contrast retains at least one common market and is identical across contexts.
